We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our Systems Biology Department at the Institute of Biomedical Genetics (IBMG), University of Stuttgart (https://www.ibmg.uni-stuttgart.de/systems_biology/). The successful applicant will study the regulatory mechanisms of alternative splicing in health and disease using a combination of kinetic modeling, bioinformatic data analysis and/or AI. The appointment will initially be limited to 3 years.The University of Stuttgart is one of the leading technical universities in Germany and provides an inspiring interdisciplinary environment at the interface of biology and engineering. The Systems Biology group combines mathematical modelling with state-of-the-art experimentation and is part of the newly founded Institute for Biomedical Genetics as well as the Stuttgart Research Center Systems Biology (SRCSB), one of the largest German interfaculty infrastructures for systems biological research (https://www.srscsb.uni-stuttgart.de/).A core focus of our group is the quantitative investigation of alternative splicing, a fundamental regulatory mechanism essential for maintaining normal cellular physiology and development, while its dysregulation often leads to disease pathogenesis and therapy resistance. Combining multi-omics profiling, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning, we have derived quantitative principles governing how alternative splicing is regulated by cis- and trans-acting factors, genetic variants and cellular context (see e.g., Kristofori et al., Nucleic Acids Research 2026; Li et al., Cell Systems in press; Prieto-Garcia et al., Science 2024; Cortés-López et al., Nature Communications 2022; Enculescu et al., Biophysical Journal 2020; Braun et al., Nature Communications 2018). We will continue to apply this integrated strategy to dissect disease-relevant splicing perturbations, with a particular focus on cancers and disorders linked to defects in splicing machinery components.in splicing machinery components.We offerA PhD student position initially for 3 years (65% E13)Interdisciplinary education within the SRCSB, the SimTech excellence cluster (https://www.simtech.uni-stuttgart.de/) and the Graduate Academy of the University of Stuttgart (https://www.gradus.uni-stuttgart.de/en/)Priority access to high-performance computing resourcesA vibrant, interdisciplinary, and collaborative research environmentDevelop quantitative models of alternative splicing regulation providing mechanistic insights into perturbed splicing decisions and splicing fidelity in cancer cells (see e.g., Kristofori et al., Nucleic Acids Research 2026; Prieto-Garcia et al., Science 2024; Braun et al., Nature Communications 2018)Process raw sequencing data (e.g., short- and long-read RNA sequencing), then perform comprehensive downstream analyses and data visualizationEmploy machine learning and AI techniques to train kinetic models on quantitative experimental data.Collaborate closely with experimentalists and theoreticians within or outside the groupParticipate in teaching in systems biologyMaster's degree (or equivalent) in computational biology, bioinformatics, physics, mathematics, molecular biology, informatics, or a related fieldStrong skills in programming and numerical computation, e.g., Matlab, Python, R or JuliaEnthusiasm for basic research questions and the ability to solve problems independentlyExcellent communication skills and good team spiritFluency in spoken and written EnglishExperience in quantitative systems biology research, particularly in the context of RNA biology or alternative splicing, is beneficialPlease send a single PDF file containing:A motivation letter including a description of previous research experiencesA full CVA list of publications (if applicable)Scans of academic degrees (e.g. Abitur & Master degree)Contact details of two refereesStarting dateAs soon as possibleClosing dateApplications will be ...

jobs.description: #WeAreIn for jobs that impact everyone's life. What if your ideas could change the way the world connects, powers up, or thinks? Lastly, you listen actively to the customer and consider his point of view, thoughts, and ideas.- A degree in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, or a similar field- At least 6 years of working experience in Physical Design handling highly complex SoCs, with sound experience in Synthesis, Place & Route, and Timing Closure and involvement in FINFET technologies- Very good knowledge in Synopsys and Cadence Toolset in the RTL2GDS domain- Know-how in technical leadership in physical design projects - Sound programming skills and knowledge in scripting languages like Tcl, Perl, or Python- Basic experience in RTL coding- Understanding of** Functional Safety** will be a benefit- Excellent written and spoken English#WeAreIn for driving decarbonization and digitalization.As a global leader in semiconductor solutions in power systems and IoT, Infineon enables game-changing solutions for green and efficient energy, clean and safe mobility, as well as smart and secure IoT. jobs.description: Munich School of Politics and Public PolicyThe Munich School of Politics and Public Policy (HfP), with its affiliation to the Technical University of Munich (TUM), deals with the multifaceted interactions between politics, society, business and technology in research, teaching and practice. It was established by the Bavarian State Parliament on the basis of a separate law.The Chair of European and Global Governance investigates the causes and consequences of delegation of power to international organizations, European integration, multilateral governance, China’s influence in global economic governance, geopolitics, transatlantic relations, and disruptions in politics and technology. Another area of research is on accountability in the digital age. Theoretically, it draws on and combines approaches from international relations, international political economy and European integration theories. Methodologically, it draws on a plurality of approaches, notably qualitative methods. Your future responsibilities:- Conducting interdisciplinary research and teaching in European and Global Governance, with a focus on: - International Organizations- International Political Economy- European Integration- Advanced Qualitative Methods- Contributing to joint academic publications and the preparation of third-party funding applications in collaboration with Prof. Dr. E. da Conceição-Heldt.- Teaching and supervising undergraduate and graduate students.- Supporting the Chair in administrative, research- and teaching-related activities.Your profile:- Outstanding doctoral degree in Political Science, International Relations, or International Political Economy.- Academic advising and teaching experience on qualitative methods.- Ability to work in an international team.- English and German language proficiency. - Sufficient language skills in German for independent teaching (please indicate proficiency).- Successful record in third-party funding acquisition is an asset.- Excellent academic record with visible international publications is an asset.Our offer:- This three-year research position provides the opportunity to pursue a postdoctoral qualification at the Munich School of Politics and Public Policy at the Technical University of Munich, one of Germany's leading research universities.- The estimated starting date is April 1, 2027.- Remuneration will be in accordance with the German public service pay scale (collective agreement for state-level public servants, TV-L) at the E-13 level.Interested? We look forward to receiving your application!Please apply via our online application portal and upload your complete application documents, including:- cover letter explaining the motivation for the application- curriculum vitae (comprising a maximum of 10 pages, including a list of major publications)- academic certificates- short teaching proposal- one selected publication- letters of recommendation, may be requested during the selection processPlease address your application to Prof. Dr. E. da Conceição-Heldt and submit it no later than January 15, 2027.The position is suitable for applicants with severe disabilities. Severely disabled applicants will be given preference in the case of otherwise substantially equal suitability, qualifications and professional performance.The Munich School of Politics and Public Policy strives to increase the proportion of women. Applications from women are therefore expressly welcome.All applications received by January 15, 2027 are assured full consideration. Additional information, including letters of recommendation, may be requested during the selection process.Ergänzende Informationen:Nur schwerbehinderte oder ihnen gleichgestellte PersonenHomeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung
